full_judgment:
Abdur Rahman Chowdhury, J.—These two matters arise out of an application for bail filed by accused Basanta Kumar Das Chowkidar alias Basanta Kumar Das. He facts leading to these two rules are that upon a petition of complaint lodged by one Md. Reas Uddin Pramanik against the accused-petitioner and two other police constables, the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Bogra took cognizance of the case against the accused petitioner, while referring the case against the two police constables to the Superintendent of Police for taking depart-mental action. The accused petitioner was remanded to custody by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate and his prayer for bail was also rejected by the Sessions Judge, Bogra where upon he moved this Court and obtained the present rule. No ad interim bail was however rented to him. While issuing the rule, we also issued a suo moto rule to show because why the order dated 2.10.79 passed by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Sadar, Bogra referring the case of the two accused constables to the Superintendent of Police, Bogra for taking departmental action, should not be set aside and a direction given for proceeding against the two police constables in accordance with law. Thereafteron 9.4.80 while in the midst of hearing of the rule we issued another Sou moto rule upon the Sub-Divisional Magistrate to show cause why appropriate action under the law should not be taken against him for acting contrary to the direction of law in trying to save the two police constables from legal punishment and for non-compliance with the specific direction issued by this Court. 

 3. We have perused the petition of complaint and it appears that a prima facie cognizable offence was disclosed against the two policemen. From the petition elf complaint it was evident that the offers alleged against the two police contains were more serious in nature than the offence alleged against the Chowkidar and the two policemen were accused not only of rape but also of kidnapping the son and the daughter of the complainant. We are, therefore, satisfied that a prima fact case has been made out against the two police constables on the allegations made in the petition of complaint and we accordingly set aside the order passed by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate forwarding their case to the Superintendent of Police for departmental action and direct that cognizance be taken against the two police constables. The Sub-Divisional Magistrate is further directed to take necessary steps for ascertaining the correct identity of the two police constables and then proceed against them in accordance with law. 

 4. In obedience to the suo moto rule issued by this Court, the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Bogra appeared in person and has tendered unqualified apology and expressed his repentance for the actions taken. We have given our due and anxious consideration in the matter. There was no legal justification for the action taken by him in referring the case of two policemen to the Superintendent of Police for departmental action when a prima fade case of cognizable offence was disclosed against them. But since the two police constables were not properly identified in the petition of complaint, the scope for some confusion in the matter cannot altogether be ruled out. Moreover, we have also noted that in his affidavit there was no attempt by Sub-Divisional Magistrate to justify the impugned action. In such view of the matter we accept the unqualified apology and the expression of repentance and regret and exonerate him with a warning that while exercising judicial powers he must be careful and diligent. 

 6. As regards the prayer for bail of the accused-petitioner Bashanta Kumar Das Chowkidar the learned Counsel has submitted that he has been in custody since 2nd October, 1979. The petition of complaint discloses that the offence of rape and kidnapping Was allegedly committed by the two police constables while the Chowkidar acted as an abettor and it was he who led them to the place of occurrence. In view of his long detention we are inclined to take a lenient view and we direct that petitioner Bashanta Kumar Das Chowkidar and Bashanta Kumar Das be enlarged on bail to the satisfaction of the Court where the case is pending. He must, however, apply for bail afresh as and when the matter is sent up before the Sessions Judge and the learned Sessions Judge shall decide his case for bail on merit. 

 7. The rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 332 of 1979 and the connected suo moto rule are accordingly made absolute. The impugned order forwarding the case of the two policemen to the Superintendent of Police for departmental action is hereby set aside and the Sub-Divisional Magistrate is directed to take cognizance in the matter, under the appropriate law against the two police constables and proceed in accordance with law.
